claim: A structured second look at a held diagnosis (list findings for, against, expected-but-missing, then alternatives) raises human diagnostic accuracy by a small to moderate amount on average (pooled g 0.20 to 0.38), but most trials are vignette-only and many come from one lab network.
agent_test: Run plain answer vs structured second look (for/against/missing/alternative) at matched total tokens on a diagnosis set with hard cases; report net change, not only fixes.

claim: The benefit depends on difficulty and expertise: experts gain on complex cases and not on simple ones; novices show the reverse or no gain. Later studies do not all reproduce the pattern (family-practice residents gained on simple cases too; dermatology students gained more on easy cases).
agent_test: Stratify items by first-pass difficulty (for example agreement across samples); compare always-revise against revise only on hard or low-agreement items.

claim: Plain instructions to slow down, be careful, be analytic or avoid bias do not raise accuracy (speed vs reflect instructions N=204: 44.5 vs 45.0 percent; cognitive forcing training N=191: no effect).
agent_test: Compare a generic 'think carefully and double-check' prompt to no prompt at equal tokens; expect no gain.

claim: Free, self-directed second looks barely help: residents revised 8 percent of diagnoses and the score moved 1.20 to 1.22 of 2; what is missing is knowledge.
agent_test: Let the agent choose when to revise; log revision rate and net wrong-to-correct vs correct-to-wrong flips.

claim: A second pass that only returns to the case gives about the same small gain (0.22 to 0.26, N=167) as a for/against search; content of the reflection did not matter on very hard cases, and there was no no-second-pass control, so a pure repeat or time effect is not excluded.
agent_test: Arms: re-read case only; for-only; against-only; both; and a no-second-pass arm. Same token budget.

claim: Directed analytic search (three diagnoses, evidence for and against) did not beat first impression (N=393, F=2.44, P=.12). The DR authors reply that hypotheses must emerge one at a time from the findings, so this bounds the procedure rather than refuting it cleanly. Lambe 2018 (N=186) also found no gain in final diagnosis.
agent_test: Compare differential-list-first with hypothesis-one-at-a-time-from-evidence reflection at equal tokens.

claim: Reflection counters availability bias from recent look-alike cases, but samples are small and the reflection phase always followed the first diagnosis on the same cases, so a repeat effect is mixed in.
agent_test: Inject a prior-similar-case distractor into context; compare no reflection, reflection, and plain re-diagnosis.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Content knowledge, not process, protects against bias: one week of look-alike contrast practice with feedback made residents resist bias (0.40 vs 0.24, N=91), and extra reflection helped only with that knowledge.
agent_test: Give the agent retrieved discriminating-feature notes for look-alike pairs vs a process prompt, at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Content-focused aids help only when the content contains the answer: a differential checklist containing the correct diagnosis lifted accuracy 0.49 to 0.75; a checklist without it gave 0.43.
agent_test: Supply a candidate list that does or does not contain the truth; measure harm when it does not.

claim: Structured reflection while practising cases hurts at once and helps a week later (0.48 vs 0.62 immediate; 0.66 vs 0.48 delayed), replicated with transfer to adjacent diseases in the same lab; transfer did not replicate in novices (floor).
schema_part: memory/learning (across tasks, not within a run)
agent_test: After a case, store a for/against reflection note and test on later look-alike cases against storing the answer only.

claim: Guidance beats free reflection: cued or modelled reflection beat free reflection (p<.001), replicated by an independent group; faded examples equal cued reflection in advanced students (expertise reversal).
agent_test: Give the agent a fixed reflection template vs open 'reflect' at equal tokens.

claim: Reflection does not fix calibration: confidence and calibration were unchanged (dermatology, N=61) and overconfidence rose on hard cases; eye-tracked residents reported 64 to 67 percent confidence whatever their accuracy.
schema_part: G (do not use self-confidence as a stop rule)
agent_test: Check whether stated confidence predicts first-pass and post-revision correctness; compute calibration before and after revision.

claim: Intrinsic LLM self-correction without an outside signal lowers accuracy (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after five calls); earlier gains came from oracle labels deciding when to stop (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3 with oracle). Update (gap search): the sign depends on the prompt. A prompt that presumes an error cost GPT-4 18 points on CommonsenseQA (84.11 to 66.34) while a neutral prompt left it at 84.60; an untreated Gemini 1.0 Pro changed 15.8 percent of right MATH answers to wrong and 4.6 percent of wrong to right.
schema_part: S8/G (verify by external check, not self-judgement)
agent_test: Compare model-judged revise with a code or tool check that triggers revision; at equal tokens report net flips.

claim: Medical QA self-reflection loops (up to 10 steps) did not reliably beat chain of thought (GPT-4o MedQA 87.80 to 88.80; HeadQA 91.39 to 90.57; PubMedQA 70.80 to 69.00); over 85 percent of items needed no extra reflection. Update: the same pattern holds for reasoning models in medicine, where forced Wait re-thinking gave minimal gain and sometimes broke correct answers (m1).
agent_test: Replicate on our diagnosis set with a code-judged stop rule against a model-judged stop rule.

claim: Prompting LLMs to imitate clinician reasoning styles does not help: GPT-4 MedQA chain of thought 76 vs differential 78 (+2.2, p=.24), Bayesian 72; GPT-3.5 differential 38 vs 46 (p<.001).
agent_test: Run differential-first prompt vs plain chain of thought at equal tokens on the target benchmark.

claim: External, verifiable feedback (tools, retrieval, tests, separate fact-checking questions) makes LLM revision work (CRITIC +7.7 F1; CoVe factored FACTSCORE 55.9 to 71.4; Reflexion AlfWorld +22), while physician-judged DERA summaries improved but open-ended MedQA did not.
agent_test: Verify with independent sub-questions answered without seeing the draft (factored) vs joint verification, at equal tokens.

claim: Adding critic agents improves diagnosis from known biased misdiagnoses (top-2 0/80 first pass to 61/80 in the best GPT-4 framework), but first-pass accuracy was zero by selection and no equal-token single-agent second-pass control exists. Update (gap search): matched-budget studies outside medicine find single-agent CoT-SC or one reasoning pass equals or beats same-model debate (d01, d03, d05); in medicine MedAgents beats few-shot CoT+SC by only 1.3 points (GPT-4) with no token match (d06), and MDAgents beats CoT-SC with 9.3 vs 6.0 calls (d07). Multi-model mixing, not critique, looks like the driver (d04).
agent_test: Single agent with a devil's-advocate pass vs multi-agent, matched tokens, on cases with natural first-pass accuracy.

claim: LLMs show human-style bias under bias-inducing prompts, and instruction-level debiasing recovers only part of the loss (BiasMedQA drops 10 to 26 points by model; radiology authority cue -21 to -45 points; one-shot mitigation recovers 4 to 25).
agent_test: Inject authority, anchoring and recency cues; compare a generic debias warning with a content-specific re-examination.

claim: LLMs under-gather evidence and close early when evidence must be sought: accuracy falls 12.75 points from full context to active evidence seeking (468 cases, 15 models); VivaBench top-1 0.35 interactive vs 0.69 full information.
agent_test: Test a forced 'what is still missing' check before the final answer in an interactive diagnosis task at equal tokens.

claim: Giving physicians an LLM did not improve their reasoning score (76 vs 74, adjusted +2, CI -4 to 8) though the LLM alone scored 92; reading AI text moved answers (27.6 percent changed, 2.81 percent harmful flips).
agent_test: Not testable on a single agent; informs how revisions are presented.

claim: Self-verification prompts raised precision but not sensitivity in psychiatric vignettes (PPV 0.534-0.779, p=.007), and on code-status extraction reflective self-review hurt a 27B model while only a weak 8B model gained from a reviewer.
agent_test: Gate verification by first-pass uncertainty or model strength; measure over-calling and net flips.

claim: An unstructured challenge to an LLM diagnosis (Are you sure?) does net harm: 10 LLMs, 120 vignettes, 28,800 responses; accuracy 51.8 to 42.2 percent; 544 right-to-wrong flips vs 198 wrong-to-right; one model lost 36.4 points. Math shows the same: an untreated model flipped 15.8 percent of right answers to wrong and 4.6 percent of wrong to right.
schema_part: S8 guard (keep first answer unless new evidence)
agent_test: Log both flip directions for every S8 pass; accept a change only when it cites a new finding. Report the harmful-to-helpful flip ratio per condition.

claim: How the second look is worded decides its sign. A prompt that presumes errors (find problems) lowered GPT-4 CommonsenseQA from 84.11 to 66.34; a neutral check kept it at 84.60. Models fix an error shown as someone else's but not their own (64.5 percent blind spot over 14 models); appending Wait removed 89.3 percent of that gap. No diagnosis-domain test exists.
agent_test: Compare three S8 wordings on a diagnosis set at equal tokens: presume-error, neutral check, and first answer framed as a colleague's claim. Report net flips.

claim: At matched budgets, a pure self-refinement or same-model debate pass usually loses to sampling more first passes and voting: no MAD method won over 20 percent of 36 settings against CoT; self-refinement stayed below CoT on MMLU-Pro (CoT 64.3, SC 68.7); single-agent matched or beat multi-agent at equal thinking tokens. Mixing different models is the exception (mixture of agents 71.4).
schema_part: S8 vs sampling baseline (G on spend)
agent_test: Always run an equal-token CoT-SC arm next to any S5/S8 test; credit S8 only for the margin above it.

claim: In medical QA the multi-agent gain over a voted single agent is small and unmatched: MedAgents GPT-4 average 86.7 vs few-shot CoT+SC 85.4 and zero-shot CoT+SC 83.0; Smit 2024 found medical sets favour Medprompt and SC over debate; MDAgents routing by complexity beat CoT-SC with 9.3 vs 6.0 calls (MedQA 88.7 vs 83.9).
agent_test: Replicate MDAgents-style complexity routing with a cheap gate (sample agreement) at equal tokens against always-revise and never-revise.

claim: Reasoning-model internals do not make the scaffold second look redundant, nor clearly useful: reflection words appear in base models and do not track accuracy (R1-Zero); medical accuracy flattens above about 256 to 512 thinking tokens on routine items and around 4K on harder sets; forced Wait re-thinking in medicine gave minimal gain and broke correct answers; R1 got 93 of 100 MedQA cases and the authors list anchoring and too few alternative diagnoses among causes of its 7 errors.
agent_test: On a reasoning model, compare thinking budget B vs thinking budget B/2 plus a structured S8 pass at B/2, measuring net flips and accuracy.

claim: Verbalized LLM confidence is a weak gate for revision; sample agreement is better. In diagnosis scenarios sample consistency gave ROC AUC 0.66 to 0.79 while verbalized confidence consistently overestimated. Hidden-state probes reach AUC 0.7 to above 0.9 on math and logic but need model access.
agent_test: Gate S8 by disagreement among 3 to 5 first passes vs verbalized confidence vs always; compare accuracy and harmful flips at equal tokens.

claim: Independent groups (McMaster, Toronto) show that a structured verification pass after the expert's own reading reduces errors (checklist: 0.29 vs 0.03 errors corrected per ECG, 15 experts) and that an analytic re-read instruction raises ECG scores (F=15, p<.0001), while customised strategy-switch instructions and plain slow-down do not (F=0.22; 44.5 vs 45.0). These are small and ECG-based.
agent_test: Use a fixed analytic verification step placed after the first answer rather than adaptive mode-switch prompts.

claim: Alternatives supplied late in the process added about as much to getting the correct diagnosis into the differential as alternatives supplied early (+8 vs +7 percent, N=190 across experience levels), so the strict bottom-up order claimed by the deliberate-reflection authors has no independent support, and no independent test refutes it directly either.
agent_test: Compare listing alternatives before vs after the first committed hypothesis; measure presence of the right answer in the list and final accuracy.

claim: No trial of structured reflection with patient outcomes was found. Reviews list 28 intervention studies (mostly early-career doctors, vignettes) and only 13 of 87 debiasing studies in health targeted professionals. Training-curriculum studies measure knowledge tests, not diagnoses.
agent_test: State in the schema notes that the second look is supported by vignette evidence only.
